messages.author: 0b46b709ed258edc
messages.subject: AKDE vs MKDE
parts:
Hi Chris (or anyone that has knowledge on this subject),

I have a non-code-diagnostic question.

I recently came across the Benhamou (2011) paper on the MKDE and Biased Random Bridges (BRB). On the surface, it appeared that this method was appropriately accounting for autocorrelation by modelling the movement process with realistic options (unlike Brownian motion).  However, the results of the MKDE appear to be closer to the occurrence distribution rather than the range distribution. Is this true? And therefore, the MKDE does not attempt to extrapolate beyond the observed data, and therefore generally underestimates the home range (corresponding to the range distribution) with autocorrelated data? If so, was the occurrence distribution its intended purpose? Or is there a conflation problem going on here? 

Thanks for any insight.

Best,
Odd

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: AKDE vs MKDE
parts:
Hi Odd,

Yes, MKDE is an occurrence distribution, where the movement model used is a BRB, and the end result will tend to be smaller than a range estimate. Also, because some variance in the data is being modeled as drift (rather than diffusion) it should end up smaller than a regular Brownian bridge, as well.

MKDE was introduced before the range/occurrence distinction was noticed, so I'm not sure if this was the intended purpose, but an occurrence distribution would be the best use case for MKDE, regardless.

Best,
Chris
